name: Browser URL Parameters
location: Embedded within ordinary browser history URL records (see chrome-edge-browser-artifacts / firefox-browser-artifacts) - not a dedicated artifact store of its own.
purpose: Captures geolocation and network-identification clues leaked within otherwise-ordinary browser history URL parameters - for example, captive-portal sign-in redirects or a Google Maps URL containing geocode/daddr parameters revealing a searched address - that can identify connected networks and approximate physical locations.
key_fields: Mapping-service URL query parameters such as geocode=, daddr=, saddr=, ll=, q= found in History.urls-equivalent tables
Captive-portal redirect URLs recorded in ordinary browsing history, sometimes referencing an AP/SSID identifier
normal_baseline: Mapping/navigation URLs reflecting the user's genuine, expected routine locations (home, office, known travel); captive-portal redirects only for networks the user is expected to have used.
anomalies: Mapping-service URL parameters resolving to a location inconsistent with the user's claimed whereabouts at the relevant time
A captive-portal redirect URL referencing a network inconsistent with the organization's or user's known network history
Geolocation-revealing URLs clustering around a time window relevant to an investigation, such as immediately before or after a suspected physical security incident
anti_forensic_notes: This is not a dedicated artifact store - it is a byproduct signal inside otherwise-normal browsing history. Clearing browser history removes it identically to any other history entry (see chrome-edge-browser-artifacts / firefox-browser-artifacts anti-forensic notes), and there is no separate registry- or log-based backup of these URL parameters.
interpretation: Treat this as a byproduct signal inside otherwise-normal browsing history, not a dedicated artifact store of its own - review URL query strings within existing browser history data (mapping services, captive-portal redirects, etc.) for geolocation and network-identification clues rather than expecting a purpose-built artifact location.
